_note: Korean pedagogical terms that recur across both lessons. Phase 1 (Glossary) fills `th` and `vi` with the ONE agreed rendering each, then every reviewer enforces it so a term is never rendered two different ways across 258 strings. `keep_korean:true` = show the Korean form (optionally + a gloss in parentheses) rather than translating it away; that is what the lesson is teaching.

terms.concept: initial/leading consonant — the top-left slot of a syllable block
medial vowel — right of or under the initial
final consonant at the bottom of a block (formal term)
batchim — the final consonant, everyday term; MUST stay consistent with 종성 handling
Dubeolsik — the standard 2-set Korean keyboard layout (KS X 5002)
Hangul — the Korean alphabet; keep the name
keyboard home row (ASDF / JKL;); the F and J bumps
the Shift key — leave the English/symbol key name as-is per lesson convention
the Korean WPM unit labels (타=keystrokes, 분=minute) — DO NOT translate, they are being taught
